title: Monorepo Redwood Adapter: Quick Blueprint & Developer Rituals
content:
TL;DR
This is a lean internal blueprint for a "Monorepo Redwood Adapter" pattern: a small opinionated shim + dev rituals that make it easy for product teams that keep source in large monorepos to adopt Redwood SDKs with minimal friction and safe rollouts. The doc collects implementation patterns, CI expectations, telemetry contracts, rollout checklist and a minimal smoke-test matrix.

Context and motivation
- We repeatedly see friction when teams in monorepos try to integrate Redwood: long review cycles, diff hygiene concerns, local dev ergonomics, and inconsistent telemetry.
- Goal: provide a default path that is small, auditable, easily revertible, and fits monorepo ownership models (library vs service-level integration).
- Non-goal: replace bespoke integrations or create a heavy framework. Keep it < 500 lines for the shim.

Success metrics (how we'll know it's helping)
- Time-to-first-call for a new feature in a monorepo <= 2 hours (from PR to verified smoke run).
- Percentage of monorepo teams using the adapter for new integrations >= 40% in Q1 after rollout.
- Reduced SDK-related incidents in monorepo services (baseline: incidents/month -> target: -50%).

High-level pattern options (pick one as default)
1) Minimal Library Adapter (default): small wrapper pkg that exposes a narrow, team-friendly API surface (call(), stream(), embed()) and centralizes config/credential resolution.
2) Local Sidecar (optional): lightweight sidecar that offers a local TCP/HTTP shim for teams who prefer to not link runtime deps into service binary.
3) Feature-flagged Sidecar-in-Prod (for large infra teams): sidecar with control-plane flags and canary routing.

Recommended default: Minimal Library Adapter
- Why: lowest friction for CI, smaller review footprint, easier to unit-test, and follows monorepo norms (library changes instead of service-level runtime changes).
- Size target: ~200-400 LOC (excluding vendored SDK).

API surface (opinionated minimal)
- initialize(contextConfig) -> idempotent, reads credentials via standard monorepo secret resolver (env/KV).
- call(prompt, opts) -> {text, meta} (blocking), with timeout and circuit-breaker defaults.
- stream(prompt, opts, onChunk) -> pluggable stream callback, default backpressure handling.
- embed(items) -> list[vector] with batched behavior.
- helpers: telemetryEvent(name, tags), validateResponse(schema)

Configuration conventions (to reduce PR friction)
- Single config file per package: redwood.adapter.yaml (supports env refs only, no inline secrets).
- Default timeouts: 3s per request for UI flows, 10s for background workers.
- Batching policy: expose a single knob (batching.enabled = true/false) and leave tuning to Optimize team suggestions.
- Credentials: resolve from MONOREPO_SECRET_STORE or per-service KMS wrapped env var.

CI/CD expectations (must be lightweight)
- Unit tests for the adapter (mocked Redwood runtime) are required.
- Integration smoke tests: small hermetic test that runs a sample prompt against a sandbox host; 30s wall time budget.
- Linting: a specific golden file check to ensure redwood.adapter.yaml schema unchanged unless explicitly intended.
- PR template additions: checkboxes for telemetry events added, config file added/updated, smoke-test output attached.

Telemetry & contract (non-negotiable for observability)
- Events (structured): redwood.request.start, redwood.request.end, redwood.request.fail.
- Min fields on events: trace_id, repo_path (package), environment (dev/stage/prod), adapter_version, model_hint, latency_ms, token_count_estimate, error_type.
- Counters: redwood.calls.total, redwood.calls.success, redwood.calls.retry, redwood.calls.timeout.
- Sampling: 0.1% full-response capture by default (opt-in per team to increase).
- Logs: adapter emits structured logs (json) with level, short message, and trace_id; avoid dumping prompt text in prod logs—only attach redacted version.

Testing matrix (smoke/practical tests)
- Unit: mocked backend, deterministic outputs. Quick.
- Integration (CI): hits Redwood sandbox host (auth via ephemeral token). Expectation: minimal, stable prompt that asserts schema. Max 30s.
- Load sanity (optional for heavy users): run a local batcher sim at 50 req/s for 60s in a non-blocking job; ensure batching doesn't deadlock.
- Local dev: provide a dev-run script that spins up a local mock server and a dev shim so engineers can iterate with no network.

Migration/rollout checklist (phased)
Phase 0 — experiment
- Create adapter package in monorepo root under /libs/redwood-adapter-experiments.
- Add README with quick start (2 commands) and add a minimal smoke test.
Phase 1 — alpha teams
- Move adapter to canonical path /libs/redwood-adapter.
- Onboard 2 product teams as alpha; pair-program integration and collect feedback.
Phase 2 — staged rollouts
- Promote adapter changes with feature flags; default opt-in for non-critical flows.
- Validate telemetry and smoke tests in staging for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 — general availability
- Publish internal docs + examples; create a migration playbook per service owner.

Developer rituals (to reduce shipping friction)
- 15-min pairing session for first integration (engineer + SDK maintainer).
- Pre-merge checklist in PR template (telemetry, config file, smoke test, readme snippet).
- Weekly 30-min open office hours for first 6 weeks after GA.

Anti-patterns to avoid (common causes of friction)
- Checking long-lived secrets into repo. Use secret references only.
- Adding broad, runtime-visible config without migration plan.
- Shipping heavy wrappers that replicate Redwood logic — prefer thin shims that forward calls and centralize config/telemetry.

Sample minimal README (to paste into package)
1) install (monorepo): yarn workspace @redwood/adapter add @redwood/sdk
2) configure: create redwood.adapter.yaml with credential ref
3) quick run: node -e "require('@redwood/adapter').call('hi', {timeout:3000}).then(r=>console.log(r.text))"

Smoke prompts (kept stable):
- Prompt A: "Summarize the following in one sentence: 'Redwood Inference builds inference platforms.'"
- Prompt B (schema check): "Return a JSON object with keys title (string) and score (number between 0-1) for the text: 'hello'"

Known risks & mitigations
- Risk: monorepo owners require custom credential flow -> mitigation: provide a pluggable CredentialResolver interface (small, documented).
- Risk: teams bypass adapter for micro-optimizations -> mitigation: document cost and perf tradeoffs and provide Optimize team presets to tune.

Open questions (for product/infra)
- Should we maintain a canonical sidecar container image for teams that prefer that route? (infra cost vs convenience)
- What's the standard SLT (service-level test) to include in prod canaries? (will decide in SRE sync)
- Default sampling rate for full response capture — 0.1% or 1%? Ask privacy/compliance.

Next steps (owners)
- Asha: draft adapter skeleton and PR (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Jordan: define redwood.adapter.yaml schema and implement schema validation in CI (ETA: 1 week).
- Priya: create sandbox tokens and add to CI secrets (ETA: 3 days).
- Luca: prepare telemetry dashboards (initial set) and a preview grafana panel (ETA: 2 weeks).

Appendix: quick dev commands
- Local mock server: ./scripts/run-local-redwood-mock.sh (starts on 127.0.0.1:9090)
- Run smoke test: yarn workspace @redwood/adapter test:smoke --ci
- Generate telemetry schema: yarn run telemetry:generate --output=telemetry/redwood-adapter-schema.json

Notes to reviewers (explicit asks)
- Focus feedback on: API ergonomics, CI cost/latency, telemetry field set, and any security concerns re: credential resolution.
- Prefer smaller API surface even if it means adding convenience helpers later.

This doc is intentionally compact — appendices, code skeleton and a simple example app will live in the linked PR."
